verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
verse.sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
verse.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verse.translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.for_you: You spin up possibilities, and the world of trouble grows. Today, let one thing be enough.
verse.try_today: Notice one thought you feed today, and let it go.
verse.scene_line: You sit with your own mind, and it spins possibilities into worry.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
the swelling is traced to the spinning, which can be stopped

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
verse.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.
verse.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.for_you: Your mind keeps turning because it is still gripping the result of your work. Let the outcome go, and the grip loosens. Peace comes at once.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you release your grip on how a result must turn out.

why: Peace follows at once from letting go of the fruit.
peace is placed right after releasing the grip on results, not after mastering meditation
plan_v3.writer_note: Letting-go teaching for a reader who is building something. Explain it through their own situation and feeling: what is released is the grip that hurts them, never their love, their hope or their work. Never say or imply 'stop caring' or 'your hope is the problem'. Read it after the guard verse, which reassures first.

verse.speaker: Bhushunda
verse.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verse.sanskrit: किमद्य मम संपन्नं प्रातर्वा भविता पुनः । इति चिन्ताज्वरो नास्ति तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verse.line: 'What happened today? What comes tomorrow?' I don't run that fever. That's why I live well.
verse.translation: 'What has happened to me today? What will come tomorrow?' I have no such fever of worry; so I live long, free of illness.
verse.why: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

prasang.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
prasang.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
prasang.story_hook: High on a mountain lived a crow who had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall.
prasang.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

verse.for_you: You keep circling the same worry about what is happening today and what it all means. You do not need to run that fever. You can live well right now, free of illness.
verse.try_today: Let the mind rest in the fact that you are alive right now.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your own life, and Bhushunda does not ask what comes next.

why: Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
worry is called a fever he does not run

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), chapter 6: the first practice for a racing mind.
verse.line: Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch.
verse.translation: The first lesson, then, is to sit for some time and let the mind run on. The mind is bubbling up all the time. It is like that monkey jumping about. Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch. … But you will find that each day the mind's vagaries are becoming less and less violent, that each day it is becoming calmer.
verse.why: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

prasang.title: The drunken monkey: taming a restless mind
prasang.summary: The mind is a monkey made drunk by desire, stung by jealousy and possessed by pride. The first practice is to sit and watch it without fighting; each day it grows calmer. Then take up one idea and let it fill your life.
prasang.story_hook: There was a monkey, restless as all monkeys are; someone gave it wine, then a scorpion stung it, and then a demon got into it.
prasang.lesson: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

verse.for_you: You keep asking what today means and what is going on. The mind is a restless monkey. Let it jump. You simply wait and watch. Each day it grows calmer.
verse.try_today: Sit and watch the mind run without fighting it.
verse.scene_line: You sit and watch the monkey of your mind jump about.

why: calm arrives by itself, day by day

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न वैरमुद्दिपयति प्रशान्तं / न दर्पमारोहति शान्तिमेति / न दुर्गतोऽस्मीति करोत्यकार्यं / तमार्यशीलं परमाहुरार्याः
verse.line: Don't rake up settled quarrels, don't ride your pride, and don't excuse wrongdoing because times are hard.
verse.translation: He does not rekindle a quarrel that has died down, does not climb onto his pride, stays calm, and does not do wrong telling himself 'I am in a bad way': the noble call such conduct the best.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

why: A calmed enmity is left calm
Hard times are not taken as licence

story.title: Young Uddalaka sits down to meditate and his mind will not stay
story.story_hook: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
story.summary: Uddalaka is young, proud and serious. He longs for a calm mind: 'When will I rest in that stillness? When will my mind stop swinging between liking and disliking?' He sits in meditation in the forest, and his monkey-like mind runs to the objects of the senses.
story.lesson: A restless mind is not overcome by force but by patient return and clear inquiry into what one is.
story.teaser: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
story.for_you: You do not have to silence the swinging mind. You only need to return to it, gently and again. What you are is not the worry that circles.
